records.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ADOPTION AND PROJECT PERFORMANCE: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF DYNAMIC CAPABILITIES AND THE MODERATING EFFECT OF ORGANIZATIONAL AMBIDEXTERITY
records.abstract: AI has become embedded in project management activities like planning, scheduling, forecasting, risk analysis, reporting, and resource allocation and decision support. However, simply using AI is not enough for a project to have successful results. This article proposes a moderated-mediation model, whereby, dynamic capabilities discuss how AI adoption is transformed into the project performance, and organizational ambidexterity discusses the mediation's strength. Based on Dynamic Capabilities Theory and the exploration–exploitation perspective, the dynamic capabilities are viewed as sensing, seizing and transforming, and organizational ambidexterity is defined as the simultaneous engagement in explorative and exploitative activities. The study puts forth six hypotheses: (1) that the adoption of AI has a positive impact on project performance and dynamic capabilities; (2) that dynamic capabilities have a positive impact on project performance and mediates the relationship between AI and project performance; (3) that ambidexterity strengthens the dynamic capabilities–project performance relationship, and (4) that the indirect effect between dynamic capabilities and project performance is higher when ambidexterity is high. A mixed method approach with explanatory sequential design is suggested. The quantitative phase is based on a survey of project professionals and PLS-SEM, while the qualitative phase is based on semi-structured interviews that provide explanations for the mechanisms observed. The framework helps shift the focus in the field of management and project-management research, from purchasing AI to organizational skills and balancing mechanisms that can help create project value. Keywords: artificial intelligence adoption; project performance; dynamic capabilities; organizational ambidexterity; project management; mixed methods; moderated mediation

records.title: The Algorithm Will See You Now: A Theoretical Framework for AI-Enhanced Organizational Learning
records.abstract: Organizational learning has been a central theme in management research yet debates over its definition and frameworks remain largely unresolved. With the rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI), there is a pressing need to revisit how organizations create, distribute, and apply knowledge. This paper advances a reconceptualization of learning processes by integrating AI's transformative capacity to accelerate, personalize, and scale knowledge alongside its inherent risks of bias, misinformation, and eroded source credibility. Building on classic organizational learning theory, including Argyris's single and double-loop learning and March's exploration-exploitation framework, this study proposes a theoretical model that captures how AI reshapes knowledge creation, dissemination, and validation at individual and collective levels. The paper develops six theoretical propositions examining the relationships between AI integration, learning velocity, knowledge democratization, quality control mechanisms, and organizational adaptation. By reframing learning as a socio-technical capability where human judgment and AI analytics operate in tandem, this study addresses a critical gap in the literature and provides a foundation for empirical research into how organizations can evolve their learning processes in the digital era. This framework offers researchers testable propositions for examining AI's impact on organizational learning while providing practitioners with strategic guidance on implementing validation mechanisms.
